text: The morning allocation presents the case to this service as the child-workflow input of DeviationWorkflow on task queue rwb-deviation, and the placement returns as the stage outcome the parent applies; no REST operation is added and no hop is taken, so the case input and the outcome carry their field names as placeholders until RWB-P3-E1020-CON publishes them.
why: The S8 row of the connection matrix names Temporal and events to P3 and never REST, TSD S8 T5.2.1 states only that DeviationWorkflow is the child of the case started by P3, and no source publishes an operation by which the run presents a case; a REST path invented here would be a second, unsourced contract and would break the one-hop rule of DP-11.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.4 class C and R5.5 DP-11; context pack S8 connection-matrix row and service row; Architecture v5 slide 13; TSD S8 T5.2.1 and T-A.1; legacy RWB-E1-020 section 4 step 3
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-case owner, before RWB-P3-E1020-CON is tagged
impact: The story builds on Day 1 against the P3 fake, adds no REST operation, and a build that publishes a second allocation path fails the boundary test

text: The handler of a placement is the owner the fired code rule names, chosen among the queue members the P3 contract lists for the handler queue, and the choice takes the handler with the fewest open deviations in this service's own rows; no cap is applied because no source publishes a handler cap, and two handlers with the same load are ordered by their handler identifier.
why: R-DEV-03 to R-DEV-06 name the role that owns each code and give no method, TSD S8 T4 carries the same rules without a method, and the legacy method and cap of RWB-E1-020 belong to the case owner in rwb-case. queue_member and capacity_cap are P3's rows, so the candidate list arrives on the contract and the load is counted in rwb_deviation; a cap chosen by the builder would be an invented business value.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DEV-03 to R-DEV-06 and R-DEV-21; FSD S8 A2.4.3.1; TSD S8 T3.1, T4 and T6.1; context pack ownership rows; legacy RWB-E1-020 sections 4 and 11 (DF-WRK-047, DF-WRK-048)

confirm: Solution architect and the business owner of the deviation module, before the placement is built
impact: The placement answers one handler with no cap, the load is counted locally, and a cap appears only when a source sets one

text: "DEV-HANDLER" is the handler queue code in force and is read at every placement from the parameter allocation.deviation.queue.code through the parameters contract of rwb-case; a different value moves the case to that queue with no deployment, and no queue code appears in the code.
why: Legacy RWB-E1-020 section 3 records the parameter and its value as assumed under DL23, and DP-06 puts parameters in rwb-case with a client library, so the value is a row and not a constant. The queue itself is P3's recovery_case.queue_id, and this service answers the code rather than writing a queue.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-020 sections 3 and 4; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-06 and R5.5 DP-07; FSD S8 A2.4.3.1 BR-S8-004; context pack naming rules

text: This key keeps wave 1 and release 30 November 2026 (tentative) as the plan gives them, and the platform contracts behind the DP rows are wave 0 preconditions already in place, so the H row stays None and only RWB-P3-E1020-CON is carried as a class C row.
why: Template and Rules v1 R5.6 keeps the earlier W-MAP wave and R5.7 makes a story with only CON H dependencies Day 1; U7 and R7 copy a date unchanged and mark it tentative. The plan gives H = None for this split slice and every pattern dependency of R5.5 points at a wave 0 CON story, so adding it to the metadata would contradict the plan, while naming it as a precondition keeps the build honest. The service wave 2 against business wave 1 is recorded as one conflict in CG-B2-S8-011-2.

text: The event id EV-06 is published as DeviationRaised on rwb.deviation.events.v1 with rwb-case, rwb-comms and rwb-treatment as its listeners, and this story publishes no DeviationCleared because nothing is cleared at a placement.
why: The ownership map carries the ids without names and TSD S8 T0.2, T5.2.1 and T5.3 give the names, the topic and the consumer lists, so the pairing is taken from the TSD rather than invented. A placement sets a handler and moves the deviation to DEV_WITH_OWNER, which clears nothing, and EV-07 belongs to the clear path of the other stories of this service.
